hero.title: Separate Findings from Interpretation.

scenes.title: Start with source status
scenes.narration: Start with your conversation log. Label actual, planned or rehearsal material, context and source quality. Planned sessions have no findings yet. Fictional role-play can teach sorting but is not customer evidence.

scenes.title: State a finding carefully
scenes.narration: A finding should stay close to the source: one person reports checking two pages to find registration. A reported account is not independent observation of that event. Include its anonymous source code and context.

scenes.title: Label your interpretation
scenes.narration: An interpretation explains what the finding might mean: route visibility may need exploration. It is your explanation, not the person’s statement. Link it to the source and keep its uncertainty visible.

scenes.title: Test other explanations
scenes.narration: The person may have used an old link, unfamiliar event type or different device. Preserve exceptions and accounts where the current process works. Do not discard contradictions to strengthen your story.

scenes.title: Keep patterns bounded
scenes.narration: Repeated mentions may suggest a theme, but repeated notes from one source are not multiple participants. If you use counts, report verified independent sources and context, not a market-wide percentage. Do not invent counts.

scenes.title: Write the review
scenes.narration: Build your Findings and Interpretation Review with sources, findings, quality, tentative meanings, possible patterns, contradictions, unknowns and next check. These notes do not establish payment or representative demand.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Keep the source and your explanation visible.

children: A
finding
states what a source reports or what you directly observed, within its context. An
interpretation
is your explanation. A
possible pattern
is a recurring theme across identified independent sources. An
unknown
marks what you cannot establish.
Finding — fictional practice
R01 role-play notes: the fictional participant describes checking two pages for registration. This is a paraphrased reported account, not observed behaviour or real customer evidence.
Interpretation
Route visibility may need exploration. Alternative: an old link, different device or unfamiliar event context. Neither explanation is established by the practice note.
Inventory source codes, context and actual/planned/rehearsal status.
Write narrow findings with source links and source quality.
Put your explanation in a separate interpretation field.
Check independent sources before claiming a repeated theme.
Preserve exceptions, contradictory accounts and alternative explanations.
State unknowns and choose the next permitted check.

Three notes from one person remain one source. Two people mentioning something does not establish how common it is in a market. Use verified counts only with their scope and avoid market percentages from convenience interviews. Do not infer payment from praise or future preference.

Review anonymous summaries only here. Original identifiable notes and recordings belong in an approved secure system. If you have no actual research, use a clearly labeled practice review or mark findings unknown; never invent evidence to complete fields.
